text: Tuesday, after the finding: the cravat recognised, Hunter recovers
why: The murder happened Monday night (¶20, ¶32-33), so the body is found on Tuesday morning. The maid recognises the cravat (¶35) and Hunter recovers from his stupor (¶36), both stated.

text: What did the stranger want at the stable? — drug the watchman
why: ¶36 states that Hunter was certain the stranger drugged his curried mutton and so deprived the stables of their watchman. The question and its answer are both covered by the text.

text: What was in the stranger's paper? — a drug
why: This is a possibility the story has given reason to consider: the stranger offered a folded paper for the boy (¶24), the packet was visible in his hand (¶26), and the watchman was later drugged (¶36). The text never confirms the paper held a drug, but the label presents it only as a possibility.
